title: Affine-line compact support of constructible finite-coefficient sheaves
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. All derived categories below are the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine for a commutative ring $A$, let $a:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ be the projection [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $(\mathbf A^1_Y)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], placed in degree zero. Then $\mathcal H^q(Ra_!^cF)$ is constructible for every integer $q$ and every compactification $c$ of $a$.

source.place: Tag 0GKZ, label lemma-constructible-shriek-rel-dim-1; finite-ring bounded-below specialization

proof.text: Write $A$ as the directed union of its subrings $A_i$ generated by finite subsets as rings. The schemes $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i[t])$ have affine transition morphisms and limit $\operatorname{Spec}(A[t])=\mathbf A^1_Y$: a map out of the union of the rings is exactly a compatible family of ring maps, which proves this limit assertion directly. Apply constructible-module limit descent to obtain $F_i$ constructible on $X_i$ with pullback $F$. Put $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $a_i:X_i\to Y_i$, and choose a compactification $c_i$ of $a_i$ using nonemptiness of the compactification category. Its base change is a compactification of $a$. By compact-support base change, exactness of module inverse image, and compactification independence, for the compactification $c$ in the statement one has $\mathcal H^q(Ra_!^cF)\cong (Y\to Y_i)^{-1}\mathcal H^q(Ra_{i,!}^{c_i}F_i)$. Pullback preserves constructibility (apply the constructible-pullback theorem with module coefficients). Hence it suffices to treat affine bases with finitely generated integer coordinate ring. Such schemes and their finite-type schemes are Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem.

Fix such an affine $Y$. Use Noetherian induction on its closed subsets: for a closed subscheme $B\hookrightarrow Y$, consider the assertion for every constructible module sheaf on $\mathbf A^1_B$ and every compactification of its projection. Closed subschemes have finitely generated integer coordinate rings by taking quotients. Whenever an open cover is needed, choose finitely many principal affine opens inside the open subset; their coordinate rings are localizations $R_s$, generated over $\mathbf Z$ by the generators of $R$ and $s^{-1}$. It is enough to prove the assertion on a dense open of every nonempty closed $B$, since the complement is a strictly smaller closed subset. The induction starts with the empty scheme, where all sheaves and their direct images are zero. For a finite open cover constructibility is checked by refining the finitely many local strata to a finite locally closed partition, then taking their finite locally constant restrictions; this is directly the constructibility definition. For the union of a constructible open $V$ and its closed complement the same conclusion follows by concatenating their stratifications. Base change and exact inverse image identify restrictions of the output sheaves with the output for the restricted affine-line projections.

source.place: Tag 0GKZ, induction paragraph; Noetherian induction version of dimension induction

proof.text: For a nonempty closed affine base $B$, apply generic constancy with $\Lambda$-module coefficients to the constructible sheaf $F$ on $\mathbf A^1_B$. It gives a dense open $U$ on which $F$ is finite locally constant as a module sheaf. This uses the cited theorem rather than assuming that an open with image inside a stratum factors through its chosen immersion. A dense open contains every generic point of the finitely many irreducible components: its intersection with each component off the other components is a nonempty open of that irreducible component, hence contains its generic point. Let $Z$ be the reduced closed complement. Over each generic point $\eta$ of $B$, the fiber $\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(\eta)}$ has its generic point in $U$ (this is the generic point of the corresponding irreducible component of $\mathbf A^1_B$); its proper closed subset $Z_\eta$ is finite, since the primes of $\kappa(\eta)[t]$ containing a nonzero polynomial are its finitely many irreducible factors. The generic-finiteness neighborhood theorem applied to $Z\to B$ gives a dense open $V\subseteq B$ on which $Z\to B$ is finite. Here $Z\to B$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and of finite type because it is closed in the relative affine line over a Noetherian base. Cover $V$ by finitely many principal affine opens and work on each of them.

source.place: Tag 0GKZ, induction paragraph, dense lisse open and finite complement; Tag 02NW

proof.text: On each affine open $W$ of $V$, put $U_W=U\times_BW$ and $Z_W=Z\times_BW$. Restrictions of $F$ to these are constructible by constructible pullback; $F|_{U_W}$ is finite locally constant by the choice of $U$. The lisse-relative-line input proves that $R(U_W\to W)_!(F|_{U_W})$ has constructible cohomology. The map $Z_W\to W$ is finite and of finite presentation: on affine charts its finite algebra is finitely generated and the base is Noetherian, so a finite algebra presentation has finitely generated relation ideal. It is separated; on affine charts the finite-ring-map quasi-finiteness theorem gives quasi-finiteness at every point, which is quasi-finiteness of this finite-type morphism by the quasi-finite definition. Hence quasi-finite shriek constructibility proves the same assertion for $R(Z_W\to W)_!(F|_{Z_W})$. No invertibility of the order of $\Lambda$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0GKZ, final two sentences; Tags 0GKY and 0GK3

proof.text: Apply relative open-closed localization to $U_W\subseteq\mathbf A^1_W$ and its reduced closed complement $Z_W$. In its cohomology exact sequence write $A^q=\mathcal H^q(R(U_W\to W)_!F|_{U_W})$, $M^q=\mathcal H^q(R(\mathbf A^1_W\to W)_!F|_{\mathbf A^1_W})$, and $C^q=\mathcal H^q(R(Z_W\to W)_!F|_{Z_W})$. Exactness gives $0\to\operatorname{coker}(C^{q-1}\to A^q)\to M^q\to\ker(C^q\to A^{q+1})\to0$. The outer terms are constructible by kernels and cokernels closure, and $M^q$ is constructible by extension closure. Thus all output cohomology is constructible on $V$. The induction hypothesis applies to the closed complement $B\setminus V$, with its reduced structure; base change identifies its output with the restriction of the original output. Concatenating the open and closed stratifications gives constructibility on $B$. This completes the induction; step 1 then returns to arbitrary $A$, and compactification independence gives the assertion for every $c$.
